units.text: Welcome to Brussels. Over the next hour or so, we are going to tell the story of a city that has been a marsh settlement, a ducal seat, the capital of a vast empire, a battlefield, a revolution, and today the working capital of Europe.
Brussels does not look like one thing.
It is a Gothic town hall and a glass tower of the European Union.
It is a medieval square rebuilt in four years after a bombardment, and a boulevard built over a river.
It is a city where two languages share every street sign, and where nearly four in ten residents hold a foreign passport.
How did a small town on a muddy river end up here?
The answer is a story of trade, guilds, dukes, emperors, revolutionaries, and a great deal of stubbornness.
We will move in order, from the first settlement to the present day.
